editorial:
Imagine if you could record a dream or a feeling and play it back for someone else to experience exactly as you did. That is the wild idea behind this movie. You follow two scientists who build a machine that does exactly that. At first, it seems like a miracle for art and science, but things get creepy fast. The vibe is very 80s, with bright colors and a feeling of curiosity that slowly turns into a nightmare. You get to see the characters go from being excited about their invention to being terrified of what it can actually do to the human mind.

What really makes this movie work are the trippy visuals and the shocking twists. While some of the acting feels a bit dated, the plot keeps you guessing until the end. It is a bit slow in the middle, but the payoff is worth it. If you love old-school sci-fi, you should definitely check this out. It is a perfect movie for a Friday night when you want something that makes you think.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a huge twist when you find out the main character actually died long ago. He recorded the feeling of death and played it back so perfectly that his consciousness stayed trapped in the machine. He is basically a ghost made of data. In the end, the recording loops and takes over, showing that once you record the end of your life, there is no way to truly come back.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange 80s movies and mind-bending plots.
